record.paper_title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications
record.original_question: When the truth-degree set in quantitative logic is a lattice rather than [0,1], determine what the appropriate notions of measures on lattices and aggregation operators on lattices should be so that the meta-degree machinery of quantitative logic remains meaningful and useful.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.4 (S. Gottwald). Particularly, what about suitable measures on lattices; and what about aggregation operators on lattices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In quantitative (graded) logic, formulas are evaluated in a truth-degree structure, classically the real unit interval [0,1] equipped with a t-norm (or more generally a residuated structure). The "meta-degree" machinery of quantitative logic associates to each formula a numerical degree of truth (or of provability, consistency, etc.) by combining, via a measure μ on the set of valuations and an aggregation operator A, the pointwise truth values of the formula. Specifically, if V is the set of valuations, e_φ: V → [0,1] the truth-value function of a formula φ, μ a (probability or fuzzy) measure on V and A an aggregation operator [0,1]^V → [0,1], then the meta-degree of φ is obtained by aggregating the family (e_φ(v))_{v∈V} with respect to μ via A.

Now replace the truth-degree set [0,1] by a general (bounded) lattice L (for instance a complete residuated lattice). Develop the corresponding theory: namely,

(a) Define an appropriate notion of an L-valued measure on a measurable space (or on the σ-algebra of subsets of the set of L-valuations), specifying monotonicity, additivity/sub-additivity, continuity, and normalization conditions, that reduces to the classical notion when L = [0,1] and that supports a meaningful integration calculus for L-valued functions.

(b) Define an appropriate notion of an aggregation operator A: L^X → L on a lattice L, specifying the axioms (boundary conditions, monotonicity, idempotency or compatibility with lattice operations) that yield a usable class, again reducing to the standard one when L = [0,1].

(c) Show that, using these notions, the meta-degree construction of quantitative logic (truth-degree, provability-degree, consistency-degree, etc., of formulas) extends from the [0,1]-valued setting to the L-valued setting in a meaningful and useful way: i.e., the resulting meta-degrees should satisfy natural counterparts of the basic properties known in the [0,1]-valued case (logical soundness, monotonicity in the formula, behaviour under logical connectives, limit theorems, etc.).

Provide such definitions and prove that they yield a coherent extension of quantitative logic to lattice-valued truth degrees.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open research direction asking for "suitable" notions of lattice-valued measures and aggregation operators tailored to quantitative logic. While there is an extensive literature on lattice-valued measures and on aggregation functions on lattices, no canonical or universally adopted framework specifically validating the quantitative-logic meta-degree machinery in the lattice-valued setting appears to have been established, so the problem is best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: Aggregation functions on bounded lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies aggregation operators on general bounded lattices, generalizing the [0,1] case.
status_evidence.claim: Aggregation operators on lattices are an active research topic but no canonical framework tied to quantitative logic has emerged.

status_evidence.title: Lattice-valued measures and integrals
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses generalized measure theory and integrals taking values in ordered structures.
status_evidence.claim: Several competing notions of lattice-valued measures exist; selection of the 'right' one for graded logic remains open.
